source.title: Benign Overfitting without Linearity: Neural Network Classifiers Trained by Gradient Descent for Noisy Linear Data
source.authors: Spencer Frei; Niladri S. Chatterji; P. Bartlett

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a related gradient-training claim for two-layer networks on a theoretical noisy, high-dimensional mixture classification problem, using logistic loss and full-batch gradient descent rather than benchmark experiments.
record.gate_note: The theorem gives an explicit training-loss and classification result under stated assumptions. It does not test CIFAR benchmarks, width thresholds, depth, shortcuts, normalization, or the learning-rate stability phenomena in the versions. Cited results from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proves interpolation and generalization guarantees for fully connected two-layer networks on a theoretical mixture distribution. V1 concerns convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/100. The paper's own results do not test that system and setting, or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove noisy-label interpolation with generalization close to the noise rate under their high-dimensional mixture assumptions, without relying on the NTK approximation. Closeness requires sufficiently large n∥μ∥⁴/p; minimax optimality up to constants in the exponent is established for random classification noise.
record.recipe_differences: The paper provides a theoretical guarantee for unregularized full-batch gradient descent on logistic loss in a two-layer network with fixed random second-layer weights and smoothed leaky ReLU activations, on a high-dimensional mixture distribution. The claim version concerns empirical benchmark networks trained with SGD or Adam.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee is conditioned on assumptions A1–A6, including high input dimension relative to sample size, bounded label-noise rate, and a fixed-step-size constraint; it allows arbitrary width and arbitrarily small initialization variance.

fits_no_version.finding: Under assumptions A1–A6, randomly initialized two-layer networks of arbitrary width attain zero training classification error and arbitrarily small logistic loss with high probability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-batch gradient descent can interpolate adversarially corrupted labels with finite-width, smoothed leaky-ReLU networks on sufficiently high-dimensional, well-separated mixture data.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3.1 bounds test error by η + 2 exp(−n∥μ∥⁴/(Cp)).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolating two-layer networks can generalize close to the label-noise rate in the specified mixture setting when n∥μ∥⁴/p is sufficiently large.

record.problems: The evidence is a theorem under restrictive distributional and optimization assumptions rather than an empirical benchmark evaluation. The authors identify the high-dimensional p ≫ n assumption as central and leave open whether benign overfitting can occur when n > p.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying result rows found. Results about initialization displacement and intermediate proof lemmas are not separate outcomes for the versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100 with SGD or Adam, including label corruption and model-size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Spurious local minima and the effect of adding student neurons in ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and training deep networks without shortcuts or normalization.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature evolution, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's supports and limits_scope labels for V1 should both be removed. Assumptions of a theorem and omitted benchmark comparisons do not themselves establish a scope limitation of V1. Initialization displacement and arbitrary-width guarantees also do not test V4 or V2.

versions.untested_parts: Tests convergence to arbitrarily small training loss and correct classification on a theoretical noisy classification distribution, but not CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels on benchmarks, or comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.

reader_labels.condition: Theorem 3.1 setting: two-layer networks of arbitrary width on the specified high-dimensional noisy mixture, under assumptions A1–A6 and the stated iteration bound
reader_labels.reason: The theorem guarantees all training examples are classified correctly with loss at most ε (R1), while bounding test error by η plus an exponentially small term (R2).
